description_full: Horizon Kinetics Holding Corporation is an employee owned investment manager. The firm primarily provides its services to high net worth individuals. It also caters to individuals, investment companies, pension and profit sharing plans, pooled investment vehicles, charitable organizations, and corporations. The firm manages separate client-focused equity and fixed income portfolios. It also manages equity mutual fund for its clients. The firm invests in the public equity, fixed income, and alternative markets across the globe. It typically invests in value stocks of small cap and large cap companies. The firm employs a fundamental analysis to create its portfolios. It conducts in-house research to make its investments. Horizon Kinetics Holding Corporation was founded in 1994 and is based in New York City with additional offices in Charlotte, North Carolina; Summit, New Jersey and White Plains, New York.

financial_summary: Horizon Kinetics Holding Corpor is a small-cap financial services business with a $354M market cap on $73M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +64% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at -42% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 42%.
The company is burning through $43M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.8%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 56% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 33% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 46% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 48% and a beta of 0.83, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.92 vs 5y 0.04), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $53K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 50% in the 2020 crash, 88% in the 2022 bear market and 85% in 2008.
val: On multiples it looks expensive against Financial Services peers: P/E 190.0 vs 12.3 (sector median).
prof: ROIC of 42% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.8%, so growth at these returns destroys value.
It runs a 42% gross margin and burns cash (FCF margin -60%).
It earns a 2% return on equity.
Operating margin is running 37pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 63.8% over 3 years, 19.2% over 5 years and 9.6% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 408%).
own: Insiders own 56.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 7%.
Insiders have only bought over the past year (22 purchases, net $138K bought).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.8% (2.7% in dividends).
It pays out 425% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 81 employees, each generates about $899K of revenue, 1.8x the Financial Services median, and revenue has grown 11.6% a year across its filed history.
